content.title: About
content.content: White rice flour, pre‑gelatinized (5914) is a finely milled rice flour that has undergone pre‑gelatinization, improving its water absorption and gel‑forming abilities. The product is gluten‑free, has a neutral taste, and is used in baking, sauces, and gluten‑free blends.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pre‑gelatinized rice flour swells quickly in cold water, making it easy to use in cold batters.
Rice flour is a staple in Asian cuisine for noodles, batters, and desserts.
Being gluten‑free, it is suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
Pre‑gelatinization enhances shelf‑life stability and improves the texture of finished products.
Rice flour has a higher glycemic index than wheat flour, so it should be used in moderation.

items.title: Rich source of carbohydrates
items.content: Rice flour provides easily digestible carbs that quickly supply energy.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Ideal for gluten‑free diets, reducing the risk of allergic reactions in celiac individuals.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie recipes.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The pre‑gelatinized structure aids digestion and rapid nutrient absorption.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Large amounts can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes, which is a concern for diabetics.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to rice, experiencing skin or digestive reactions.

items.title: Low protein content
items.content: Rice flour is low in protein, so other protein sources should be included in the diet.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Use the flour in gluten‑free baking (bread, cakes, cookies), sauces, soups, breading, and as a thickener for desserts. Thanks to pre‑gelatinization, it can be added to cold mixtures without prior heating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For long‑term storage, keep refrigerated to prevent mold growth.
